public_derivative.scope: Codex-only released execution path and deidentified metric-level sufficient data

transformations: Exported the recursive local-import closure of nommd_arena.glee_parallel plus the exact 4-module training closure imported by the promoted sequence lab.
Replaced post-launch sequence-lab tests with the tests from the lab source commit fa5d2ab534c7cc070644ebe9da29e626b7005fa2.
Removed the historical nommd-arena console-script declaration because cli.py is outside the live closure.
Extracted the selected Codex transport into nommd_arena.codex_transport and removed unselected transport backends and the historical shared package boundary.
Renamed the final deployed prompt components to canonical public filenames and removed the historical prompt-variant selector without changing the composed instructions.
Regenerated the public runtime and sequence-lab dependency locks after removing the historical transport package.
Omitted private snapshot inventories whose path listings exposed unrelated project structure; their SHA-256 identities remain recorded here and the exact inventories remain in the private archive.
Rewrote only the standalone paper evidence-ledger paths; source artifact bytes and cited private-source hashes are unchanged.
Derived a public-safe campaign-wide execution summary from the private all-history receipt and retained its source SHA-256 without journal-level paths, identifiers, or prefix inventories.

Projected held-out targets, frozen predictions, table-local anonymous group labels, rating outcomes, dossier call costs, and execution measurements into 8 compact Parquet tables sufficient for the reported estimators.

Regenerated the reversed-Persuasion held-out outputs once from hash-bound weights and corpus because no original row-level prediction file was retained; the resulting difference is below the manuscript's reported precision.

Excluded credentials, browser state, raw model corpora, learned weights, stable identifiers, messages, exact timestamps, full event journals, full cloud-call journals, superseded releases, and mutable databases including the unhash-bound opponent-timing store.
